theory.intro: A simple interest graph shows interest earned over time. Because the same interest is earned each period, the interest-time graph is a **straight line through the origin**, and its gradient represents the annual interest.
facts: $I = Prn$ produces a straight-line graph passing through $(0, 0)$ when interest is plotted against time.
The gradient of the line equals the annual interest earned, $Pr$.
A steeper line indicates a higher interest rate or a larger principal.
A graph of total investment value against time has a vertical intercept at $(0, P)$.
To find interest at time $t$, read vertically to the line then across to the vertical axis.
steps: Identify whether the vertical axis represents interest ($I$) or total value ($A$).
Locate the given time on the horizontal axis.
Move vertically to meet the line and across to read the value.
Calculate the annual rate using $r = \frac{\text{gradient}}{P}$ when required.

mastery.question_text:
Investment $X$ has $P = \$10\,000$ at $3.5\%$ p.a. simple interest.
Investment $Y$ has $P = \$6000$ at $7\%$ p.a. simple interest.
After how many years will Investment $Y$ have earned $\$1400$ more total interest than Investment $X$?

Two investments earn simple interest at $4.5\%$ p.a.
On an interest graph, their lines have equations $I = 180t$ and $I = 270t$.
Calculate the principal invested in each account.
